feedback: The confession follows the evidence I used before voting: Chip’s material denial, his own closure work, private-glass access and the false insurance date. Opening during the preview and putting stolen poison into the glass specify the action sequence, but neither supplies a new decisive premise needed to identify him. The explicit reminder that the scrap is not a fingerprint is fair, though slightly instructional for a confession. His final reflection on trusted hands connects the crime emotionally to his profession. Brie’s staff concerns and Elle’s repayment obligation continue their existing personal arcs instead of turning them into irrelevant red herrings. This felt earned and proportionate to the available evidence, with a credible motive of professional exposure rather than an unexpected late revelation.
